name: userver
listed_description: C++ asynchronous web and service framework, named in the preface as a high-speed alternative to Drogon according to TechEmpower results.
claim_text: Book says TechEmpower benchmarks list userver among high-speed alternatives to Drogon; no numbers given.
book_benchmark: None run by the book; points reader to the public TechEmpower benchmarks.
guessed_baseline: other C++ web frameworks (Drogon, Crow, Pistache, cpp-httplib) on TechEmpower plaintext/JSON/DB tests
found_in: book: Software Architecture with C++, 2nd ed. (2025), Preface, 'To get the most out of this book' (EPUB, no page numbers)

name: ffead-cpp
listed_description: C++ web application framework listed with Lithium, userver, Cutelyst and cinatra as a fast framework per TechEmpower.
claim_text: Book lists ffead-cpp among high-speed alternatives to Drogon per TechEmpower benchmarks; no numbers given.
book_benchmark: None run by the book; points reader to the public TechEmpower benchmarks. Repo README separately cites a TechEmpower rank (seen on repo page, not in book).
guessed_baseline: other C++ web frameworks (Drogon, Crow, Pistache) on TechEmpower tests
found_in: book: Software Architecture with C++, 2nd ed. (2025), Preface, 'To get the most out of this book' (EPUB, no page numbers)

name: Envoy Proxy
listed_description: High-performance proxy server written in C++ for microservice architectures; used for routing, load balancing, back pressure and as a sidecar.
claim_text: Book calls Envoy a high-performance proxy server written in C++, designed for microservice architecture.
guessed_baseline: NGINX or HAProxy as L7 proxy
found_in: book: Software Architecture with C++, 2nd ed. (2025), ch. 4, 'Back pressure pattern' (EPUB, no page numbers)

name: ScyllaDB
listed_description: Wide-column NoSQL store (C++ on Seastar) offered as an alternative to Apache Cassandra when data suits columns and joins are not needed.
book_benchmark: None; the book only lists it next to Cassandra, DynamoDB and BigTable. Repo page claims order-of-magnitude gains from shared-nothing design, no figures.
found_in: book: Software Architecture with C++, 2nd ed. (2025), ch. 4, 'Which NoSQL technology should I use?' (EPUB, no page numbers)

name: Memcached
listed_description: In-memory key-value cache used for cache-aside caching; book says such caches can be really fast and efficient, and notes it does not persist data.
claim_text: Book: cache-aside caching with Memcached, Valkey or Redis 'can be really fast and efficient'; no numbers.
found_in: book: Software Architecture with C++, 2nd ed. (2025), ch. 4, 'Cache-aside cache' and 'Which NoSQL technology should I use?' (EPUB, no page numbers)

name: NGINX
listed_description: Web server named as an HTTP accelerator that caches web server responses, often paired with Varnish.
claim_text: Book: web server caches speed up reading pages via HTTP accelerators such as Varnish, NGINX or Apache.
found_in: book: Software Architecture with C++, 2nd ed. (2025), ch. 4, 'Caching patterns' (EPUB, no page numbers)

name: Varnish Cache
listed_description: HTTP accelerator that caches web server responses in front of the origin server.
claim_text: Book: HTTP accelerators such as Varnish speed up reading web pages by caching responses.
guessed_baseline: origin web server without HTTP cache, or NGINX proxy cache
found_in: book: Software Architecture with C++, 2nd ed. (2025), ch. 4, 'Caching patterns' (EPUB, no page numbers)

name: Citus
listed_description: PostgreSQL extension for sharding, recommended because sharding can bring great performance at scale.
claim_text: Book: sharding 'can often bring you great performance at scale'; recommends Citus for Postgres.
found_in: book: Software Architecture with C++, 2nd ed. (2025), ch. 4, 'Replication patterns' (EPUB, no page numbers)

name: YugabyteDB
listed_description: Distributed SQL database recommended with Citus and CockroachDB for sharding Postgres-style workloads at scale.
found_in: book: Software Architecture with C++, 2nd ed. (2025), ch. 4, 'Replication patterns' (EPUB, no page numbers)

name: BDE (Bloomberg Development Environment)
listed_description: Mature C++ library suite listed with Boost, Folly, Abseil, Qt and EASTL as ready-made code that helps write quality software faster.
claim_text: Book lists BDE among libraries that help write high-quality software faster; no performance claim.
found_in: book: Software Architecture with C++, 2nd ed. (2025), ch. 1, 'Following the SOLID and DRY principles' (EPUB, no page numbers)
